description: Rear dormer with juliette balcony involving front roof lights and detached outbuilding at rear, ancillary to main dwelling.
decision_conditions: The proposed roof extensions due to poor design, bulk and positioning would appear incongruous and visually intrusive, particularly within views of the roofline and as such would fail to be subordinate to the host dwelling and would be out of character with the surrounding. The proposals are thereby contrary to Policies CP30 of the Core Strategy (2010), D4 of the London Plan (2021), DMD6, DMD13, and DMD37 of the Development Management Document (2014), as well as the guidance contained within the NPPF (2026).

The proposed development, by virtue of the facilities provided within the building, the independent rear access via an alleyway leading to Keston Close and lack of integration between the proposed annexe and the existing dwelling, cannot be considered to be ancillary to the main dwelling and it would form a separate and distinct independent unit of accommodation. As such, the new dwelling would detract from the established pattern of development in the area to the detriment of the character of the area. The proposal therefore would be contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policy D4 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CP30 of the Core Strategy (2010) and Policies DMD6, DMD8, DMD12 and DMD37 of the Development Management Document (2014).

In the absence of an adequate site-specific flood risk assessment, the proposed development fails to demonstrate that it would be safe from flooding and would not increase flood risk elsewhere.  The development would also result in a loss of floor storage on site, and no level for level flood compensation has been provided. As such, the proposed development is contrary to Policies SI 12 of London Plan (2021), CP28, CP29 of Core Strategy (2010), DMD 59, DMD 60, DMD 61 and DMD 63 of the Development Management Document (2014) and the NPPF (2026).
